Factor Scores and Their Prediction Errors

Source: R/latscores.R
latscores.Rd

Compute continuous factor scores from a fitted lcfa or lefa model, using closed-form weights. No numerical optimization or score Hessian is needed.

Usage

latscores(
  fit,
  data = NULL,
  method = "regression",
  se = TRUE,
  missing = "patterns",
  center = NULL,
  scale = NULL,
  do.fit = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  control = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'latscores'
se(fit, type = "prediction", digits = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'latscores'
vcov(object, person = NULL, group = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'latscores'
latInspect(fit, what = "est", sort = TRUE)

Arguments

fit

A fitted lcfa or lefa object.

data

Raw observations; NULL uses the original fitting data. A matrix or data frame is accepted. For multiple groups, use the fitting group column, or a named list of matrices/data frames (one per fitted group). Columns are matched by name. An unnamed matrix must be in indicator order.

method

One of "regression", "tenBerge", "Bartlett", "Harman", or "Green", ignoring case. "determinant", "Krijnen", and "McDonald" are aliases for tenBerge; "OLS" is an alias for Harman.

se

Logical. Store model-based prediction errors. These treat fitted measurement-model parameters as fixed; they do not include uncertainty from estimating loadings, covariances, means, or standardization constants.

missing

"patterns" uses each person's observed indicators; "complete" returns NA scores for incomplete rows without deleting them. Regression permits any pattern, including no observed indicators (the fitted latent mean). Other methods require full column rank within every scored pattern and stop if that requirement is not met.

center, scale

Optional raw-data centering and scaling constants, as vectors in indicator order (or named vectors), or lists by fitted group. Scalars are recycled. Defaults reproduce the fitted model's scale and fitted observed means, using training data, never the new scoring sample. Explicit values override these defaults: scores are computed from sweep(sweep(data, 2, center, "-"), 2, scale, "/"). For a covariance-only fit without recorded means, supply center (0 for already centered data).

do.fit

Logical. FALSE prepares the dataList and modelInfo only.

message

Logical. Print a short progress message.

control

Optional list; tol (default 1e-10) controls relative matrix rank/positive-definiteness checks. No optimizer settings are needed.

type

Only "prediction" is supported for score uncertainty.

digits

Optional rounding of the displayed SE matrices, not the stored SE vector or covariance blocks. NULL returns full precision.

...

Reserved; unsupported arguments produce an error.

object

A latscores object.

person

Optional row number within group; return its q by q prediction-error covariance. Without person, return the compact nested list of covariance blocks; case-to-pattern indices are in Optim$case_pattern.

group

Fitted group label or index; required for person in multigroup fits.

what

One of "est", "scores", "se", "vcov", "weights", "case.pattern", "structures", "param", "trans", or "model".

sort

Apply the input model's display ordering and signs.

Value

An S4 latscores object inheriting from latent, with dataList, modelInfo, Optim, parameters, transformed_pars, and extra slots. parameters$scores is the score matrix for a single group; multiple-group blocks are named scores.<group>. Optim$weights contains weight matrices by group and observed-data pattern, in model units. Optim$SE$table_se has score-shaped SE matrices, and Optim$SE$se is their labeled vector. Optim$SE$VCOV is a nested list of small prediction-error covariance blocks; Optim$SE$case_pattern identifies the block belonging to each person. extra$model retains fit. With se = FALSE, se() can compute SEs later.

Details

Write Sigma = Lambda Phi Lambda' + Theta, where Phi is latent_cov, including structural regressions when present. Scores are alpha + B'(y - mu). The full residual covariance Theta is retained.

Regression minimizes mean squared prediction error without a covariance constraint. Green minimizes its trace subject to B' Sigma B = Phi. tenBerge is the determinant-optimal covariance-preserving version given in the SAM workshop. Both preserve the fitted covariance in the population model; the covariance of a finite sample of scores generally differs. For orthonormal factors these methods coincide with Anderson-Rubin scores. Bartlett is conditionally unbiased generalized least squares; Harman is conditionally unbiased ordinary least squares.

For every method, the reported prediction-error covariance is E = (B' Lambda - I) Phi (B' Lambda - I)' + B' Theta B. The score SEs are sqrt(diag(E)), with no division by sample size. Under Gaussian regression scoring E is also the posterior factor covariance. For Green and tenBerge it is marginal prediction MSE, not an individual posterior covariance or a parameter-estimation standard error.

Only one small covariance matrix is stored per group/missingness pattern. No covariance matrix of dimension (number of people times factors)^2 is constructed. se() and vcov() use dedicated methods rather than the generic multistep/multistage parameter-estimation machinery.

Native factor order and signs are retained in all slots, as in lcfa/lefa. latInspect(..., sort = TRUE) applies the source model's display ordering and signs. se() and vcov() retain native coordinates.

The formulas require continuous responses. Ordinal/polychoric/Yule models are rejected because scoring numeric category codes is not equivalent to scoring the model's underlying continuous responses.

References

Green (1969). Best linear composites with a specified structure. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02289359

Krijnen, Wansbeek, and ten Berge (1996). Best linear predictors for factor scores. https://doi.org/10.1080/03610929608831883

ten Berge, Krijnen, Wansbeek, and Shapiro (1999). Some new results on correlation-preserving factor scores prediction methods. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0024-3795(97)10007-6

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(latent)
fit <- lcfa(HolzingerSwineford1939,
            model = 'visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
                     textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
                     speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9')
fs <- latscores(fit, method = "Green")
fs@parameters$scores
fs@Optim$SE$table_se$scores
latInspect(fs, "scores")               # Display order and signs.
se(fs)$table_se                        # Native order and signs.
vcov(fs, person = 1)                   # Small error covariance for person 1.
fs_new <- latscores(fit, data = HolzingerSwineford1939[1:5, ],
                    method = "regression")
} # }
